title: Opportunistic infections
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's infection (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for painful swallowing and esophageal symptoms.

HPI
The patient is a 77-year-old woman presenting for a follow-up evaluation of her esophagus. She was recently seen for symptoms of odynophagia. A scheduled endoscopy was performed, which confirmed the presence of Candida esophagitis. The patient reports that while she has been taking her prescribed medication, she still experiences some discomfort when swallowing solid foods. She denies any new fevers, chills, or significant weight loss since her last visit. She notes that the severity of the pain has slightly improved but remains bothersome.

Medication List
- Fluconazole 200 mg daily
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Atorvastatin 20 mg daily

Review of Systems
The patient reports no cough, shortness of breath, or chest pain. She denies any recent rashes or joint pain. She reports no changes in bowel habits or urinary frequency. She denies any dizziness or syncope.

Social History
The patient is a retired teacher who lives with her spouse. She enjoys gardening and walking. She denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Her mother had hypertension. Her father had a history of coronary artery disease.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Temperature: 98.6 F
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air

Recent Labs
White Blood Cell Count: 7.4 x 10^9/L
Hemoglobin: 12.8 g/dL
Platelets: 210 x 10^9/L
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL

Exam
The patient is a well-appearing, alert, and oriented 77-year-old woman in no acute distress. Her skin is warm and dry. Heart and lungs are clear to auscultation. Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended. Oral mucosa is moist without lesions.

Assessment
The patient is a 77-year-old woman with confirmed candidal esophagitis. She is currently undergoing pharmacological treatment. While she reports some lingering odynophagia, she is progressing toward clinical improvement.

Plan
The patient will continue her current course of fluconazole as prescribed. We will monitor her progress and reassess her symptoms at the next scheduled appointment. She was instructed to report any worsening of symptoms or high fevers immediately.

Electronically signed, E. Castillo, DO, 05/14/2026

distractors.why: Esophagitis, not only the mouth, is documented (HCC 6).
